chunks: And from him, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The servant is not made to take an oath except based on his knowledge, and it does not take effect except based on the knowledge upon which he is made to take an oath, whether he is made to take an oath or not.

key_terms.وَلَا يَقَعُ: and it does not take effect / fall upon
key_terms.يُسْتَحْلَفُ: is made to take an oath / is compelled to swear

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for an oath to be legally binding in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential nuance that an oath's binding force is contingent upon the swearer's actual knowledge (*'ilm*) of the matter, rather than mere formal declaration. It underscores the Shia legal principle that ignorance invalidates the oath's effect, ensuring justice by preventing individuals from being bound by what they do not truly know, whether the oath was explicitly requested or self-imposed. This distinction is crucial in *fiqh* for determining liability in cases of mistaken oaths or conditional vows.
